findings.reason: §22 must name the existing tokeniser owner and either reuse it or state why a new one is needed, because "extracts nothing of its own" is already not true of its tokenisation.
findings.text: §22 states its change measure "extracts nothing of its own" and reads prose from the one section reader, but the measure is a word-level sequence comparison and the package already owns one at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:477 (_longest_contiguous_word_span) tokenised by _normalised_words at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:289; as written the measure silently introduces a second word tokeniser/normaliser rather than naming the existing one, so the reuse map the section claims to satisfy was not run against it

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend write_review_sidecar with the optional field, so the payload shape keeps one owner instead of drifting across two functions.
findings.text: §23 records a refused store by "a private function beside the writer that rewrites the sidecar through the same atomic writer with store_error added", so _REVIEW_SIDECAR_NAME now has two payload-constructing writers; the section justifies keeping the layout in one module but never says why the existing public write_review_sidecar (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:798) cannot simply take an optional store_error and stay the one spelling of the sidecar payload

findings.reason: the section must name in its own text what the added public definition retires or merges, or state why nothing countable can be, per the one rule interface_budget applies.
findings.text: §23 is the only implementable section that grows a counted family: it adds the public store_delivered_reviews (public_definitions 1481 → 1482) while naming only the retirement of the private _store_delivered_plan_review in routing, which the counter does not count, and states no counted merge or retirement and no reason none can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16's one section_prose reader and §22's one coverage predicate each hide the slicing, tag-strip, snapshot recompute and threshold measure behind a small interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan extends owners rather than forking: it folds the report-root duplication into review_report_directory and the store step into plan_review.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §23 adds the counted public store_delivered_reviews and names only a private, uncounted retirement.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §22's word-level change measure proposes a sequence matcher over words without citing the existing word-sequence machinery at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:477.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §23 adds a private sidecar rewriter beside write_review_sidecar without saying why the existing writer cannot take an optional field.
